summary: Frontend-only verification of Plane Crash font fix on Home page. All target elements (hero EDICION/2026, 'SOMOS MAS QUE UN TORNEO', stat numbers 11/+1k/+100/+10k, FINALES, region title, FESTIVAL/PREMIER, footer heading, footer phone+email) correctly render with the Plane Crash grunge stencil font using the planeCrashSafe() normalizer (lowercase + accent strip). Non-target elements (logo, cursive tagline, nav links, subtitles, stat labels) still use Anton/Allura/Barlow. Other routes (/login, /admin, /cotizar) still load 200 — no regression from runtime font injection in index.js.

issues: [data-testid=hero-edition] has scrollWidth (882px) > offsetWidth (660px) at 1920px viewport — the EDICION glyphs extend slightly past their grid column, but the parent hero section has overflow-hidden so visually the text is not cropped. Pre-existing layout characteristic, not introduced by font fix; flagged for awareness only.

critical_code_review_comments: index.js font injection is correctly idempotent (early-return on duplicate id 'fsc-plane-crash-font') and uses font-display: swap — safe.
planeCrashSafe() is a pure helper applied only at render time; the Spanish-readable uppercase output is preserved visually because Plane Crash stencil glyphs at lowercase look uppercase by design.
Minor: hero-edition can scroll-overflow its grid column at 1920px; consider clamp upper bound 160px instead of 180px, or apply overflow-hidden on the column directly. Cosmetic only.
Pre-existing 401 console errors on public routes suggest the frontend triggers admin API calls without auth — should be gated to authenticated routes (not related to this change).

context_for_next_testing_agent: Plane Crash font fix verified working in iteration 29. The font is injected at runtime via /app/frontend/src/index.js because Emergent preview strips <style>/<link> from index.html. document.fonts.check confirms the font is loaded; all data-testid'd elements that should use Plane Crash do so, and all others retain Anton/Allura/Barlow. No code changes were needed during testing.
